corrections.old_text: The mission’s work involved Indigenous communities; Spanish authorities also used missions to advance territorial claims in Texas.

reference_additions.title: Mission San Antonio de Valero 3rd Site The Alamo
reference_additions.supports: Mission aims involving Indigenous people and Spanish territorial claims; competing explanations of the Alamo name; composition of the 1836 garrison and presence of families and enslaved people.

corrections.old_text: Two proposed explanations for “Alamo” are the name of the soldiers’ former company and the Spanish word for cottonwood; the name’s origin is uncertain.
corrections.new_text: Two proposed explanations for “Alamo” are the name of the soldiers’ former company and the Spanish word for cottonwood; the name’s origin is uncertain.

corrections.old_text: The 1836 garrison included Tejanos as well as Americans, Anglo-Texians, and other European immigrants; families and enslaved people were also inside.
corrections.new_text: The 1836 garrison included Tejanos as well as Americans, Anglo-Texians, and other European immigrants; families and enslaved people were also inside.
